entries.actual_retained_proof: Use the trace's stalk description, weighted base change, the cartesian lower-shriek diagram, then passage to complexes.
entries.comparison_basis: These are relative-dimension-zero weighted trace maps. The structural morphism of a curve is not locally quasi-finite; the result supplies no degree-two geometric trace, no all-r duality/perfection or finiteness of the target groups.

entries.actual_counted_target: For Noetherian affine finite-dimensional Y, torsion Noetherian Lambda, and finite-type locally constant F on an open U of A^1_Y, Rf_!F has constructible cohomology sheaves.
entries.actual_retained_proof: Reduce Lambda to an ell-primary factor and U to a connected component, use a finite étale covering and trace splitting, then a finite constant filtration and the constant case.
entries.comparison_basis: It is a constructibility/finiteness-type pushforward theorem, not a perfect pairing theorem. Its finite-cover/trace proof resemblance to Milne's route is not semantic identity. Taking Y=Spec k gives no H^(2-r) dual or perfect specific pairing.

entries.actual_counted_target: For nonempty smooth proper equidimensional X/k of dimension d, a k-linear trace on H_dR^(2d)(X/k), unique up to multiplication by a unit of H^0(O_X), makes the de Rham cup-product pairings perfect.
entries.actual_retained_proof: Use the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence/extreme-degree Hodge duality, induct over truncations of the de Rham complex, and compare the displayed wedge-product exact sequences.
entries.comparison_basis: The coefficients/cohomology theory are de Rham k-vector spaces and the geometry is proper with untwisted global de Rham cohomology. Milne's target ranges over open regular curves, finite local systems, finite torsion coefficients and a specific normalized étale trace. Setting d=1 does not change those missing hypotheses/data.
entries.simple_specialization_relation: Dimension-one specialization gives proper de Rham duality only; no automatic all-field finite-coefficient étale/local-system comparison is supplied by this counted primary.

entries.actual_counted_target: Given data D0,D1,D2' satisfying axioms A1-A7 of the stated field-valued Weil-style cohomology setup, axiom A (Poincare duality) follows with trace lambda from A6.
entries.actual_retained_proof: For nonempty smooth projective equidimensional X, use the diagonal cycle class to construct unit/counit on graded F-vector spaces and verify the triangle identities via the diagonal/conormal argument.
entries.comparison_basis: This is a theorem about a cohomology theory already satisfying the listed cycle/Kunneth/trace axioms, on smooth projective schemes with field-valued graded cohomology. It does not establish those axioms for all finite Z/n local systems on arbitrary open curves and does not assert Milne's compact-support all-r pairing.
entries.simple_specialization_relation: Taking dimension one is not enough; substituting Milne's finite local-system theory would require additional axioms/results not claimed by this counted primary. Those are not assumed for deduplication.

entries.counted_primary_label: Demarche-Harari jep129 Proposition4.1 AMM complex, source1266-1272; full proof1274-1311
entries.actual_counted_target: Over nonempty U in a smooth projective geometrically integral curve over a FINITE field, bounded complexes C of finite flat commutative group schemes have perfect profinite/discrete-torsion pairings H_c^(2-i)(U,C) x H^i(U,C-hat) -> H_c^3(U,G_m) ~= Q/Z, with C-hat=Hom-complex(C,G_m[1]).
entries.actual_retained_proof: The length-zero finite-flat AMM theorem is an explicitly cited input; the counted author proof extends it to bounded complexes using the kernel/cone devissage, dual exact triangles and the five-lemma. Retained context includes the topology and pairing construction.
entries.comparison_basis: Its base field is finite and the arithmetic trace has total degree three into Q/Z; finite-flat fppf bounded-complex duality is broader in coefficients but a different arithmetic scope. It does not directly specialize to arbitrary algebraically closed k (including characteristic zero) with geometric degree-two Z/n trace.
entries.simple_specialization_relation: Concentrating C in one degree only recovers its finite-field arithmetic base case. Passing to an algebraic closure with all geometric pairings would need additional descent/limit/comparison work not a stated simple specialization here. Do not recast 14.7 as 14.16.
